name: gate5-jit-cache-under-rank-pressure
description: Concurrent JIT compilation at 64+ ranks. Report 4.7: with Triton and Inductor caches on Lustre the concurrent writes lose races, a rank reads a partial entry and raises JSONDecodeError, that rank dies, and the rest hang at the next collective. A container whose defaults put these caches on Lustre fails this at scale while passing every small-scale test.

gates.name: jit_cache_passed
gates.note: Every rank compiled cleanly and every rank reported.

gates.name: no_missing_ranks
gates.note: A rank that wrote no record died before reporting. This is the specific shape of the reported failure, and it is why each rank writes its own file before the barrier -- reporting only through a collective would produce nothing in exactly this case.

gates.name: no_cache_corruption
gates.note: Ranks that hit JSONDecodeError or another partial-read error class.

gates.name: no_failed_ranks
gates.note: Ranks where any shape failed to compile, for any reason.

gates.name: post_compile_barrier_ok
gates.note: The collective the report says hangs once a rank has been lost. If the job is killed by its time limit instead, this gate is absent rather than false -- and a missing value counts as a failure, so the hang is still caught.

gates.name: all_ranks_reported
gates.note: Guards the test itself: the reported corruption needs 64+ ranks, so a run with fewer has not exercised the condition regardless of whether it passed.

gates.name: cache_entries_created
gates.note: Guards the test itself: confirms compilation actually wrote cache entries. Zero would mean the workload never compiled and the test proved nothing.
